title: Host template
description: One physical host in Node Exporter Full's order: summary gauges, one panel per resource, then CPU and memory, system, temperatures, fans, power, SMART, storage, network and logs, as far as the host reports them. Generated by hosts.py from templates/host.json; do not edit the generated file. docs/design/host-monitoring.md.

panels.title: NetBox
panels.description: This host's NetBox device record, read at view time. The NetBox cell links to the record.

panels.title: Pressure
panels.description: Share of the last 5 minutes some task waited on CPU, memory or I/O (Linux pressure stall information).

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Share of all cores busy (not idle), averaged over the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: Load
panels.description: Five-minute load average over the core count: 100 % is one runnable task per core.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: MemTotal minus MemAvailable: what the kernel could not free without swapping.

panels.title: Root disk used
panels.description: The host's main writable filesystem: / on the NUCs (Proxmox's local storage), /var on the Talos Pis.

panels.title: Hottest sensor
panels.description: The highest reading of every temperature sensor the host reports.

panels.title: Cores
panels.description: CPU cores the kernel reports.

panels.title: RAM
panels.description: Total memory.

panels.title: Root disk
panels.description: Size of the main writable filesystem, the one the Root disk used gauge reads.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the host last booted.

panels.title: Platform power
panels.description: RAPL psys: the processor platform's draw (CPU, iGPU, memory controller), not the whole box at the wall.

panels.title: CPU clock
panels.description: Current clock averaged over the cores. The governor lowers it when idle; under load, a clock below the CPU clock panel's maximum means the Pi is throttling on heat.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Where non-idle CPU time goes, as a share of all cores. iowait is time idle while waiting on disk.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Used is MemTotal minus MemAvailable; cache is reclaimable. Swap is the zram device (compressed RAM).

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Bits per second per physical interface and bridge (container and tunnel interfaces left out): sent above zero, received below. On a NUC, vmbr0 carries the guests' traffic over eth0, so the two overlap.

panels.title: Filesystems used
panels.description: Used share of each disk-backed filesystem (ext4, xfs, vfat, btrfs).

panels.title: CPU utilisation
panels.description: Average across all cores, and the busiest single core.

panels.title: Load
panels.description: Run-queue length averages against the core count.

panels.title: Pressure stall
panels.description: Share of time some task waited on each resource (waiting), or every task did (stalled). Sustained memory or I/O pressure is the early sign of an overcommitted host.

panels.title: CPU clock
panels.description: Lowest, average and highest core clock against the maximum the governor allows.

panels.title: Paging
panels.description: Pages swapped in and out per second, and major page faults (a page read back from disk). A Pi has no swap, so its swap lines sit at 0.

panels.title: OOM kills
panels.description: Processes the kernel's out-of-memory killer ended in each interval. Should stay at 0.

panels.title: Memory breakdown
panels.description: Where the memory goes, from /proc/meminfo. Active and Inactive split the same pages a second way (recently used or reclaimable), so they overlap the other lines. Committed (dashed) is what every process has been promised; above total memory, the host relies on processes never touching all of it.

panels.title: Context switches and interrupts
panels.description: Per second, across all cores.

panels.title: Processes
panels.description: Runnable and blocked (waiting on I/O) processes, and processes forked per second.

panels.title: File descriptors
panels.description: Open file handles across the host. The kernel limit is left out: on a NUC it is effectively unlimited.

panels.title: Clock offset
panels.description: The kernel's estimate of its clock's offset from the time source, and its maximum error. Certificate checks, log timestamps and etcd all assume clocks in step, so both should stay small.

panels.title: Board
panels.description: Thermal zones the firmware exposes: acpitz is a NUC's board sensor and x86_pkg_temp its CPU package; cpu-thermal is a Pi's SoC.

panels.title: Drive
panels.description: NVMe sensors from the kernel's hwmon driver and the composite reading smartctl reports.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Package and per-core temperatures from coretemp.

panels.title: Fan speed
panels.description: Fans the board exposes to Linux through hwmon.

panels.title: Power by zone
panels.description: RAPL energy counters as watts. Platform (psys) contains the package; the package contains the cores and the integrated GPU (uncore).

panels.title: Energy, last 24 h
panels.description: Platform (psys) energy over the last day.

panels.title: Overall health
panels.description: The drive's own self-assessment (smartctl -H). Failed means it predicts its own failure: replace it.

panels.title: Critical warning
panels.description: NVMe critical-warning bitmap. Any non-zero bit is a warning from the drive.

panels.title: Percentage used
panels.description: Vendor estimate of rated endurance consumed. 100 is end of rated life, not failure.

panels.title: Available spare
panels.description: Spare blocks left; the drive warns below its own threshold.

panels.title: Media errors
panels.description: Unrecovered data-integrity errors. Should stay at 0.

panels.title: Power-on time
panels.description: Total hours the drive has been powered.

panels.title: Data written per day
panels.description: Host writes to the drive, the figure endurance ratings are quoted in.

panels.title: IOPS
panels.description: Completed reads and writes per second, per disk.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Bytes read and written per second, per disk.

panels.title: Latency
panels.description: Average time per completed read and write.

panels.title: Busy
panels.description: Share of time the disk had at least one request in flight.

panels.title: Queue length
panels.description: Average I/O requests in flight per device.

panels.title: Filesystem free
panels.description: Free bytes per mounted filesystem.

panels.title: Packets
panels.description: Packets per second per physical interface and bridge: sent above zero, received below.

panels.title: Errors and drops
panels.description: Packets per second the interface dropped or received in error. Should stay at 0.

panels.title: TCP connections
panels.description: Established connections and sockets in TIME_WAIT.

panels.title: TCP retransmits and resets
panels.description: Segments retransmitted, resets sent and retransmission timeouts, per second.

panels.title: Log lines by level
panels.description: Log lines per interval, by level: syslog priority (0 emerg … 7 debug) for journald, level for Talos.

panels.title: Logs
panels.description: The host's own logs: journald from a NUC's Alloy, Talos machine logs for a Pi. Filter with the Contains box.
